editorialFindings.substantiveReview: The pro reconstruction joins shared interests, impartial justification, correction and protective rights. Its reinforcements separately test public reasons, institutional error correction and the inference from equal vulnerability to rights. The con reconstruction joins divine image, common nature and enemy care while preserving secular cooperation. Its reinforcements test the powerless case, intergenerational obligation and doctrine against Christian institutional failure. All ten premises make distinct steps; the six reinforcing arguments offer actual inferences rather than provenance launchers, and both conclusions preserve the source-grounding dispute.
